New in version 18: the win chance is honest now. It used to be too timid: when the app said a team was 65% to win, that team won 75% of the time, and when it said 85% the team won 95% (592 games of last season's second half, readings from tip-off through three quarters). The app counted simulated games whose final margins swing far wider than real games do. The chance now comes from the projected final margin and from how far real games swing from that minute on; in the closing minutes it is still the count of simulations, which knows the score and the clock exactly. On the same 592 games: said 65%, won 63%; said 75%, won 76%; said 85%, won 83%. On these 121 games: said 65%, won 60%; said 74%, won 68%; said 85%, won 85% (before: 71%, 84% and 94%). Scored the way forecasts are scored (the squared gap between the chance and what happened, lower is better), tip-off went from 0.213 to 0.182 on these 121 games, level with the books' own chance (0.184), and halftime from 0.160 to 0.143.

Also new in version 18: a closer projected final score. Before a game the app's own total ran low and missed by more than the books' total does, so the projected total now leans on the books' line until the game has shown its own pace (fully from nine minutes in). For the winning margin, the books' spread shared across the time left beat the app's own estimate at every moment of a game, and an early lead usually gives about a fifth of itself back by the end; both are inside the projected final now. On these 121 games the total lands 3.3% closer at tip-off (13.8 points off; the books' line itself is 13.8 off) and the margin lands 4% closer at tip-off, 6% closer after one quarter, 7% closer after 18 minutes and 4% closer at halftime. On last season's 592 games: total 4.7% closer at tip-off, margin 5% closer at tip-off, 8% closer after 18 minutes and at halftime, 6% closer after three quarters. One moment went the other way on these 121 games: after three quarters the margin was 1% further off. Player numbers were tested with the same book information and did not get closer (less than 0.2% either way), so they are left exactly as they were.

Also new in version 18: the number shown for points before the tip and at halftime, and for rebounds from the end of the first quarter to halftime, sits a little closer to the middle of the simulations, where results land most often. Points land 0.2% closer at tip-off and 0.3% closer at halftime on these 121 games (0.15% and 0.14% on last season's 592, 0.5% and 0.3% on the 20 games played since), rebounds 0.1 to 0.3% closer. A small gain, kept because all three sets of games agree.

From version 17: every made three is counted. The play-by-play feed writes about one made three in ten without the words "three point" (for example "makes 25-foot running jump shot"), and the app was missing those: a player's 3PM count during a game could read one short, and the 3PM numbers ran low. Checked against the official box score of every player in this season's first 154 games: made threes now match for 100% of 3,019 player-games (89% before). On these 121 games 3PM lands 2.5% closer at tip-off, 8% closer at halftime, 25% closer after three quarters and 45% closer with six minutes left than version 16 did. The 592 games of last season's second half show the same (2%, 9%, 27% and 49%). Points, rebounds, assists and minutes did not move: they never depended on that wording.

Also from version 17: the live numbers no longer shift at fixed moments of the game clock when nothing has happened. The biggest was at 27:00 of game time, where the minutes of every other player moved by a minute or more in one second. The lessons from halftime now blend into the lessons for the middle of the third quarter between 25:00 and 27:00. Around that stretch minutes land 1.8 to 4.7% closer on 296 games of last season's second half and 0.3 to 0.7% closer on this season's 121, and points, rebounds and assists follow. Smaller steps at the opening tip, 3:00, 15:00, 21:00 and 33:00 are gone too, with accuracy the same or slightly better at each of them.

If you mark a player OUT during a game (say he went to the locker room), he now stays at what he has and his minutes go to his teammates; before, the app still gave him some. A book line a player has already passed no longer shows as an edge. And an app left open overnight moves to the new day by itself and reads last night's games before it makes tonight's numbers, so a back-to-back is never missed.

From version 16: role anchors. The app's minutes used to be too spread out: a high number finished lower and a low number finished higher, at every stage of a game. Each number is now pulled toward what a player in that role normally plays: tonight's starters, the bench, who is on the floor right now, and his own pace tonight. With every change in this list together, minutes land 21% closer at tip-off and 13 to 20% closer in the first quarter than the app as it was on this season's 121 games; points 3.6% closer at tip-off.

During a game a player still waiting to check in keeps the same kind of number as before tip-off: what he does if he gets in. Six minutes in, minutes land 20% closer and points 3.9% closer (121 games).

Late in a decided game the app reads who is actually on the floor. When the reserves are finishing the game, the regulars on the bench are done for the night and the reserves play it out. With three minutes left, minutes land 16% closer.

A lopsided score now costs a player more the more he usually plays, smoothly, instead of one rule for starters and one for everybody else. At halftime his first-half minutes count for more than before.

Before lineups post, deep-bench players get a number too (two of every three players who had no number and then played 10+ minutes were deep bench), and minutes nobody was going to play are no longer handed to teammates. Minutes land 15% closer before lineups, points 2.4% closer. That was measured with every absence known in advance; before lineups post the phone only has the injury report, so the gain there can be smaller.
Tonight's starting five is inside every number from the moment lineups post. A reserve who starts gets his extra minutes, and a usual starter left out of the five is cut and flagged.
How crowded tonight's rotation is counts too: when several players are out, or everyone is back, minutes are not shared out evenly.

Points, rebounds and assists follow the minutes. Through the third quarter points land 1 to 3.9% closer and rebounds 0.4 to 3.9% closer on these 121 games; in the last six minutes the gain is small (about half a percent on points). The 592 games of last season's second half, which the lessons never saw (the new inputs were picked with those games in view), show the same at every stage from tip-off on: version 16 against version 15, minutes 3 to 12% closer, points up to 2%, rebounds up to 2.2%, assists up to 1.4%.

The projected final score ran 2 to 5 points low during games. A check learned from complete games now corrects half of that through the third quarter. Tested on 585 of last season's games that were not used to set its strength, the final score landed 0.6 to 3.5% closer at every moment from six minutes in to the end of the third quarter, and never further off. Player numbers are not touched by it.

What is left is mostly the bounce of the game. With the real minutes known in advance, points would still miss by about 4 at tip-off. A second learning stage that looks at the whole game state got points, rebounds and assists no closer before and early in games, and at most about 1% closer at a few later moments. The app's numbers close in on the final line as the game goes: about 3.2 points at halftime, 2.2 after three quarters, 1.2 with six minutes left.
The lessons built into the app come from 3,709 regular-season games across four seasons, through Nov 9. Every plus edge shown is saved and graded on this phone: see EDGE RECORD above.
